doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: Playing with Thad Jones: no rehearsal, learning his tunes by ear
summary: Thad Jones gave no instructions; Rydin prepared by learning his songs from records. Rowe asks about Jones leaving the States.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Did any of those fellows, Thad or Pepper, tell you something useful about accompaniment?

Yes. Playing with Thad Jones was very special. Because he also didn’t want to rehearse. And the first time I played with him I asked him, “What do you want to play?” “Well, we’ll find out” he said. He didn’t say anything what to play. So we went up on stage and you know he talked to the audience. He was very good at introducing and making everyone feel good. He said, “We’re going to start up with —” “Now’s the Time.” Of course he picked songs that in his opinion we should know. Like also, since I got this gig, of course I prepared myself, so I learned his songs, like “Three and One” and “A Child is Born,” and “Quietude.” So I learned some of his songs to prepare.
How did you go about learning those songs? By ear?
Yes by ear, by listening to records of his.

Yeah. He was so respected. We’re the same age. When I was in college we just ate those big band records up, the state-of-the-art sort of. And everybody was shocked in the jazz community when he just up and left the States.
Did he ever talk about that?
